# Jeet Kune Do Legacy Academy

> Jeet Kune Do (Bruce Lee's martial art) and practical self-defence classes in Maidstone, inner-west Melbourne, Australia, taught in Bruce Lee's direct lineage by Sigung Ricardo Vargas. Teens (14+) and adults; complete beginners welcome; the first class is free.

## Key facts

- **Official name:** Jeet Kune Do Legacy Academy (short: JKD Legacy). Website: https://jkdlegacy.com.au
- **Address:** Unit 6 / 72-80 Hampstead Rd, Maidstone VIC 3012, Australia (inner-west Melbourne, near Footscray, Maribyrnong and Sunshine)
- **Phone:** 0459 785 073 · **Email:** jkdaustralia@gmail.com
- **Group classes:** Tuesday & Thursday 7:00–8:00 pm, Saturday 9:30–10:30 am (60 minutes each). Private lessons by appointment (60 minutes; price on request).
- **Who:** teens from 14 and adults. No kids' classes. Group classes train barefoot in sports clothes.
- **Sparring:** only at intermediate/advanced level, supervised, never compulsory.
- **How to start:** leave your details at https://jkdlegacy.com.au/free-trial → Sigung Vargas calls within 24 hours → first class free.
- **Prices (AUD, Melbourne):** 5 classes $175 · 12 classes $350 · Monthly Unlimited $240 · 3-Month Unlimited $650 · enrolment fee applies · no contracts.
- **Getting there:** free parking at Hampstead Rd; bus 406 (stop Wattle Rd/Hampstead Rd). Students come from Essendon, Moonee Ponds, Avondale Heights, Brunswick, Broadmeadows, Footscray, Sunshine.
- **Reviews:** 5.0 stars from 24 Google reviews (Oct 2026).
- **Head instructor:** Sigung Ricardo Vargas — second-generation Jeet Kune Do instructor, personally trained and certified by Sifu Jerry Poteet and Sigung Richard Bustillo, both direct students of Bruce Lee. Full instructor certification 2015; U.S. Martial Arts Hall of Fame Outstanding Martial Artist of the Year 2013; 30+ years of practice; Master's in Theology and Philosophy. Opened the Adelaide Kwoon in 2011.
- **Curriculum:** Foundation (12-week rotating beginner module, start any week) → Progression (Jun Fan kickboxing, wooden dummy, grappling & clinch, five ways of attack, chi sao, sparring methods) → Mastery (private mentorship).

## Guides

- [What Is Jeet Kune Do? A Clear Guide to Bruce Lee's Martial Art](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/what-is-jeet-kune-do): Jeet Kune Do is the martial art Bruce Lee founded and named in 1967. The name means "the way of the intercepting fist". Rather than a fixed style, it is a set of principles: intercept attacks, move with economy and directness, train across kicking, punching, trapping and grappling ranges, and keep only what works.
- [Your First Jeet Kune Do Class: What to Expect](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/first-jeet-kune-do-class): Your first Jeet Kune Do class is a free 60-minute session for beginners. Wear sports clothes; group classes train barefoot. Expect a warm-up, the on-guard stance, footwork, the straight lead punch and controlled partner drills. You don't need to be fit, sparring is never compulsory, and the minimum age is 14.
- [Jeet Kune Do vs Wing Chun: what's the difference?](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/jeet-kune-do-vs-wing-chun): Wing Chun is a traditional Southern Chinese kung fu system built on centreline structure, forms and close-range trapping. Jeet Kune Do is Bruce Lee's method, developed after he trained Wing Chun under Ip Man: it keeps centreline and trapping ideas but adds boxing and fencing footwork, lead-side strategy, interception, kicking range and grappling, and rejects fixed forms.
- [What is the best martial art for self-defence? An honest comparison](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/best-martial-art-for-self-defence): There is no single best martial art for self-defence. The best choice trains against resisting partners, covers striking, clinch and ground ranges, keeps techniques simple under stress, is taught by a qualified instructor and is one you can attend regularly, all built on awareness, avoidance and de-escalation first.
- [Self-defence for women: what actually works](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/womens-self-defence-what-works): Self-defence for women works best in layers: awareness and avoidance first, clear boundaries and verbal de-escalation next, then a few simple physical skills such as palm strikes, elbows, knees, escaping grabs and getting back to your feet, all aimed at creating distance and getting away. Regular training builds these far more reliably than a one-off seminar.
- [How to choose a self-defence class in Melbourne (a checklist)](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/how-to-choose-self-defence-classes-melbourne): To choose a self-defence class in Melbourne, start with your goal, then check the instructor's lineage and credentials, class size, whether there's a trial class, contract terms, sparring policy, age range, timetable and travel time. Avoid lock-in contracts, safety guarantees and 'secret deadly techniques'. Pick a good school you'll actually attend every week.
- [Is Jeet Kune Do effective in a real fight?](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/is-jeet-kune-do-effective): Jeet Kune Do can be effective in a real fight when it is trained against resisting partners, not only in pre-arranged drills. Its strengths are interception, simple direct techniques, lead-side striking, footwork and moving between kicking, punching, trapping and grappling ranges. Real self-defence still starts with awareness and avoidance; physical technique is the last resort.
- [Starting martial arts as an adult: is it too late?](https://jkdlegacy.com.au/blog/starting-martial-arts-as-an-adult): No, it is not too late. Adults can start martial arts at any age and build real skill, fitness and confidence. Start at your own pace, tell your instructor about any injuries and choose a school with a clear beginner program. Jeet Kune Do suits adults because it values timing and efficiency over flexibility and athleticism.
